name: Contractile cardiomyocyte
short_description: The actual heart muscle cell: a branched, striated cell about 100-150 um long with usually ONE central nucleus, sarcomeres running Z-disc to Z-disc, T-tubules entering at the Z-disc, mitochondria filling roughly a third of its volume, and - its defining feature - intercalated discs whose fascia adherens, desmosomes and connexin-43 gap junctions bind and electrically couple it to its neighbours so the whole myocardium beats as one.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Exactly the house look - muted dusty educational palette, thin clean outlines, soft distinct fills per structure, neutral dark-charcoal background reaching all four edges, no border, mat or sheet-on-a-surface, no baked text. Science checks out: the cell is short and stocky and BRANCHES into a Y at both ends, four neighbouring myocytes meet it end to end and every one of those contacts is a dark step-like transverse INTERCALATED DISC carrying teal connexin-43 gap-junction plaques, warm-ochre desmosome plaques and a broad sage fascia-adherens band; a long cutaway shows parallel myofibrils with cross-striations in register (darker dusty-rose A bands, pale cream I bands), pale-blue T-tubule collars entering in the middle of the I band i.e. at the Z-disc, a pale lilac sarcoplasmic-reticulum mesh sleeving the myofibrils, dense rows of amber mitochondria filling every channel between them, and ONE oval blue-violet nucleus in the MIDDLE of the cell in a myofibril-free clearing. None of the 'do NOT draw' items: not an unbranched multinucleate skeletal fibre, no peripheral row of nuclei, no smooth-muscle spindle, no dendrites/axon/myelin, no motor end plate, no discs along the flanks. Two minor teaching caveats recorded rather than re-rendered: the slate line the model drew in the middle of each A band reads as an M line (the Z-disc is represented by the T-tubule collar, which is why the SVG labels the two together), and the gap junctions sit on the same disc plate as the desmosomes instead of strictly on its longitudinal step faces. Chosen as the SVG label base)

sem.1: partial (gemini-3-pro-image; correct false-colour surface-only SEM of branched striated myocytes with teal step-like intercalated-disc collars and T-tubule mouth dimples, but it breaks the house framing rule: the specimens lie on a pale rectangular slab/sheet with visible straight edges and corners, i.e. a plate-on-a-surface, and two fibres of nearly equal weight compete for the eye instead of one dominant cell)
sem.2: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; re-prompted for a continuous substrate running off all four edges and a single dominant specimen. One cell now clearly dominates, lying diagonally and forking into an unmistakable Y; its surface shows the gentle regular transverse rippling of the sarcolemma over the sarcomeres plus regular rows of small round T-tubule mouth openings, and every branch tip ends in a raised, deeply interlocking, finger-like teal-grey INTERCALATED DISC collar clearly different in relief from the smooth fibre. Correctly shows no internal organelles, no nucleus and no cutaway - SEM sees only the outside. Continuous granular mid-grey substrate fading into dark charcoal, no slab edge, no border, no baked text or scale bar)

3d.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Natural, believable biological tints, neither near-monochrome nor neon: translucent pink sarcolemma with subsurface scattering, deep-rose myofibrils with pale cream I bands and slate banding in register, pale-blue T-tubule collars, lilac sarcoplasmic-reticulum tubes, glowing amber mitochondria in rows between the myofibrils, ONE blue-violet nucleus in the middle of a spindle-shaped myofibril-free clearing. The cell branches into a Y at both ends; the near intercalated disc is modelled as a pronounced staircase-shaped transverse junction with interlocking finger-like relief carrying teal connexin-43 gap-junction plaques, gold desmosome plaques and a sage fascia-adherens band, and further discs appear on the far branches. Clean seamless dark studio background edge to edge, no border, no text)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; used as final on first attempt. Warm mottled aged paper with foxing fills the ENTIRE frame corner to corner - no mat, frame, drop shadow, deckled edge or sheet-on-a-surface - with a soft grey wash halo laid directly on the paper behind the subject. Fine ink linework over rich translucent washes: a stocky diagonal cell branching into a Y at both ends, dark step-like transverse ink lines for the intercalated discs at every branch tip, and at the near disc a sage fascia-adherens band with teal gap-junction plaques and ochre desmosome dots. The painted cutaway shows deep-rose A bands alternating with pale cream I bands in register, pale-blue T-tubule collars sitting in the middle of the I band, a lilac sarcoplasmic-reticulum wash, abundant ochre mitochondria in the gaps, and ONE oval violet nucleus in the MIDDLE of the cell. No text, no signature, no border)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Cardiac muscle histology 400x.jpg", CC BY-SA 4.0, Cheroske - a genuine 400x light micrograph of a longitudinal section of myocardium. Viewed at full resolution it is unmistakably CARDIAC and not skeletal muscle: finely cross-striated fibres that visibly branch and interlock, oval nuclei sitting in the MIDDLE of the fibres rather than in a peripheral row, and dark, slightly zig-zag transverse lines stepping right across several fibres - the intercalated discs. No baked-in text, scale bar, border or watermark in the source. Cleaned for display with edit_image.py (gentle recompose plus a small local-contrast lift, original haematoxylin colouring preserved, nothing invented). Honest caveat: at light-microscope resolution an intercalated disc is only a dark line - its three constituent junctions (fascia adherens, desmosomes, connexin-43 gap junctions) are ultrastructural and are NOT resolvable here, so they appear only in the illustrated styles. Two other candidates were rejected during the search: Commons "Glanzstreifen.jpg" kept a baked-in magnifier inset and leader lines through two cleaning passes, and "Histology of cardiac muscle.jpg" turned out to be a hand-drawn student sketch. No skeletal muscle was passed off as cardiac)
decision: use as final on first attempt; branching, intercalated discs with all three junction types, sarcomeres in register, T-tubules at the Z-disc, one central nucleus, mitochondria ~a third of the interior. Chosen as the primary SVG label base (13 labels)
